name: adjective plain and polite
english: Says something is X, casually or politely.
use: The base of every description. Casually an i-adjective stands alone (takai!) and da is often dropped (kirei!); politely add desu.
formation: i-adjectives: plain as is (takai, ii), polite + desu (takai desu, ii desu). Na-adjectives and nouns: plain + da (kirei da, gakusei da), polite + desu (kirei desu, gakusei desu).

example.ja: この店、ちょっと高いね
example.english: This place is a bit pricey, huh.

examplePolite.romaji: kono omise wa chotto takai desu ne
examplePolite.ja: このお店はちょっと高いですね
examplePolite.english: This shop is a little expensive, isn't it.

notes: Never put da after an i-adjective (takai da ✗); casually just say takai.

name: adjective past
use: Saying how something was: oishikatta, tanoshikatta. yokatta on its own also means 'I'm glad' or 'what a relief'.
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add -katta (takakatta); ii → yokatta. Na-adjectives and nouns: + datta (kirei datta, gakusei datta). Polite: -katta desu, or deshita after na-adjectives and nouns.

example.ja: 昨日のラーメン、めちゃおいしかった

examplePolite.romaji: kinou no raamen, totemo oishikatta desu
examplePolite.ja: 昨日のラーメン、とてもおいしかったです
examplePolite.english: The ramen yesterday was very good.

notes: Polite past is -katta desu, not -i deshita (takai deshita ✗).

name: adjective negative
use: Everyday 'not': samukunai?, amari suki ja nai. Often softened with sonna ni or amari.
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add -kunai (takakunai); ii → yokunai. Na-adjectives and nouns: + ja nai (kirei ja nai, gakusei ja nai). Polite: -kunai desu, ja nai desu or ja arimasen.

example.ja: そんなに高くないよ、大丈夫
example.english: It's not that expensive, it's fine.

examplePolite.romaji: sonna ni takakunai desu yo, daijoubu desu
examplePolite.ja: そんなに高くないですよ、大丈夫です
examplePolite.english: It's not that expensive. It's fine.

notes: ja nai? with a rising tone means 'isn't it?' (ii ja nai? = that's great, isn't it?), not 'it isn't'.

name: adjective negative past
use: Saying something wasn't so: anmari oishikunakatta. Usually softened with anmari or sonna ni.
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add -kunakatta (takakunakatta); ii → yokunakatta. Na-adjectives and nouns: + ja nakatta (kirei ja nakatta, gakusei ja nakatta).

example.ja: 映画、あんまり面白くなかった
example.english: The movie wasn't all that good.

examplePolite.ja: 映画はあまり面白くなかったです

notes: ii changes to yo- here too: yokunakatta, never iikunakatta.

name: probably / right?
use: Guessing (ashita wa ame deshou) and checking that you agree (ii deshou?). Casual speech shortens it to desho and daro.
formation: Plain form + deshou or darou: takai deshou, ii deshou. Na-adjectives and nouns drop da: kirei deshou, gakusei deshou.

example.romaji: kore, kawaii desho? kinou katta n da
example.ja: これ、かわいいでしょ?昨日買ったんだ
example.english: Cute, right? I bought it yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kore, kawaii deshou? kinou katta n desu yo
examplePolite.ja: これ、かわいいでしょう?昨日買ったんですよ
examplePolite.english: Isn't this cute? I bought it yesterday.

notes: Rising deshou? asks you to agree; falling deshou is a guess. darou is mostly male or written; most people say desho casually.

name: adjective te-form
english: Links descriptions (X and Y), or gives a reason.
use: Stringing descriptions: yasukute oishii (cheap and tasty). Also a reason: samukute nerenakatta (too cold to sleep).
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add -kute (takakute); ii → yokute. Na-adjectives and nouns: + de (kirei de, gakusei de). Verbs link with their te-form, as in the table (tabete, itte).

example.ja: あの店、安くておいしいよ
example.english: That place is cheap and tasty.

examplePolite.romaji: ano omise wa yasukute oishii desu yo
examplePolite.ja: あのお店は安くておいしいですよ
examplePolite.english: That restaurant is cheap and good.

notes: Don't join adjectives with to (yasui to oishii ✗); to only joins nouns.

name: becoming (-ku naru)
english: Becomes X; the -ku / ni part is also the adverb form.
use: For changes: samuku natta, jouzu ni natta. The same -ku / ni form works as an adverb: hayaku, kirei ni.
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add -ku (takaku naru); ii → yoku naru. Na-adjectives and nouns: + ni (kirei ni naru, gakusei ni naru).

examplePolite.ja: 急に寒くなりましたね
examplePolite.english: It's suddenly turned cold, hasn't it.

notes: naru is for things that change; suru is for changing something yourself (heya o kirei ni suru = tidy the room).

name: before a noun
english: Describes a noun directly: an X thing.
use: Constantly, to describe things and people: takai mise, kirei na hito, gakusei no toki.
formation: i-adjectives go straight before the noun (takai hon, ii hito). Na-adjectives add na (kirei na hito). Nouns add no (gakusei no toki).

example.romaji: kinou, sugoku kirei na hito mita
example.ja: 昨日、すごくきれいな人見た
example.english: I saw a really good-looking person yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou, totemo kirei na hito o mimashita
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、とてもきれいな人を見ました
examplePolite.english: Yesterday I saw a very beautiful person.

notes: Some words end in -ei or -i but take na: kirei na, yuumei na, not kirei hito.

name: adjective if
use: Conditions about qualities: takakattara kawanai. yokattara (if you like) is a very common polite offer.
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add -kattara or -kereba (takakattara, takakereba); ii → yokattara, yokereba. Na-adjectives and nouns: + nara or dattara (kirei nara, gakusei dattara). Verbs use -tara, as in the table (tabetara, ittara).

example.romaji: takakattara, betsu no mise ni shiyou
example.ja: 高かったら、別の店にしよう
example.english: If it's expensive, let's go somewhere else.

examplePolite.romaji: takakattara, betsu no omise ni shimashou
examplePolite.ja: 高かったら、別のお店にしましょう
examplePolite.english: If it's expensive, let's try another place.

notes: yokattara is less 'if it's good' than 'if you'd like' (yokattara douzo = please, help yourself).

name: looks (adjective)
use: Reacting to what you see: oishisou! (looks good!), tanoshisou, genki sou.
formation: i-adjectives: drop -i, add sou (oishisou); ii → yosasou, nai → nasasou. Na-adjectives: + sou (genki sou). Verbs use the -masu stem, as in the table (tabesou, furisou).

example.ja: わあ、これめちゃおいしそう!

examplePolite.ja: わあ、とてもおいしそうですね

notes: kawaisou means 'poor thing', not 'looks cute'. And plain form + sou da is hearsay: takai sou da = I hear it's expensive.
